Thanks Aleksandar — welcome, and thanks for the attachments. Quick responses below and a short checklist of next steps so we can complete PO provisioning from our side.

Short answers:
- PO routing: For services to EU subsidiaries we generally issue POs from "Redwood Inference GmbH" (Germany) when the contract is with an EU entity and VAT is applicable; we issue from our US entity when the contracting party is Redwood Inc and the customer is billed by Redwood US. I'll confirm the exact legal entity once Priyom checks the commercial contra.
- Reverse charge on XML: We prefer an explicit reverse-charge tag and a VAT amount = 0.00, plus the supplier VAT ID (if available) in the invoice header. That format works best with our AP import.

Immediate next steps (what I'll do):

I'll attach the checklist now.

Hi team — adding some specifics from our finance policies to avoid rework on invoices/POs.

1) VAT ID expectation: If Global Merchant can supply an EU VAT registration (e.g., DE/VAT number) or a local GSTIN, include it in the <SupplierID> header. If the supplier is not VAT-registered in the country of supply, then include the supplier country and a note: "Non-resident supplier — reverse charge applies."

2) PO entity mapping: See the attached PO_entity_mapping_table.csv. Map the "Billing Entity" field on your onboarding form to one of the Redwood legal entities listed in the first column. Common mappings:
   - Services to EU HQ / recurring subscriptions -> Redwood Inference GmbH (DE)
   - One-off professional services purchased by US legal entity -> Redwood Inc (US)

3) Invoice XML schema: We can ingest either:
   - VAT element present with amount=0 and <TaxType>ReverseCharge, or
   - Omit VAT element but include <TaxNote>Reverse charge — art. 196</TaxNote> plus <SupplierVAT> tag.

If you can update the sample invoice and re-send, we'll validate it against our import rules.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Manager (AP)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PO_entity_mapping_table.csv

Couple of practical points from tax ops:

- Withholding: If Global Merchant is an overseas service provider without a US tax presence, we typically do not withhold US taxes for services rendered to our US entity. However, if the payment is made to a non-EU bank account and the country of supplier is subject to local withholding, we may need copies of the tax residency certificate.
- Fiscal representation: For some EU countries (e.g., Spain, Italy), if Global Merchant requests Redwood to act as fiscal representative (rare), that introduces extra invoicing fields and a fiscal rep contract. Avoid doing that unless necessary.

Action requested from GM: please confirm supplier VAT registration scope (list of countries where registered) and the preferred bank beneficiary country. We'll flag any withholding risk and instruct AP accordingly.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Tax Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
